title: Tobin and the Wandering Bell
markdown:
High up in the Moonfold Mountains, where moonbeams played tag with the snowy peaks, lived a young wizard named Tobin. His heart was as bright as a freshly polished star. His wand was a perfectly straight twig from a Whispering Willow, and it hummed secrets when the wind blew.

Every day Tobin practiced in his cozy workshop, where jars of dried moon petals lined the shelf and a tinkly practice bell sat ready on the desk. He would flourish the twig and say, “Abracadabra! Twinkle-dee-doo!” Sometimes sparks flew just right and painted little shimmering rainbows. Other times they fizzled like a sleepy firefly that had decided it was far too cozy to be bright. Squeaky never minded the fizzles. He only minded if the cheese got cold.

Nestled close to Tobin’s warm robes was Squeaky, a tiny mouse with fur like moonbeam dust and the twitchiest whiskers in the mountains. While Tobin practiced, Squeaky found the sunniest spots and nibbled crumbly cheese. He loved the smell of dried moon petals and fizzing star-dust. He loved being close, just in case a spell went wobbly.

Then one day something quite strange happened.

Ding-dong! But not from here.

It was not Tobin’s tinkly practice bell on the desk. It did not sound like the workshop at all.

“That’s odd,” Tobin mumbled. His brow furrowed like a wrinkle on a surprised mushroom. He listened with his pointy wizard ears.

Ding-dong! But not from here.

This time it came from behind a big mossy rock that looked like a sleeping giant. Then, as if playing hide-and-seek, ding-dong from high up in a fluffy white cloud. The bell was ringing in all the wrong places, like a giggling echo that could not find its way home.

Tobin scooped Squeaky into his pocket among spare spell scrolls. “We’re going on an adventure, Squeaky. We have to find this wandering bell.”

Squeaky’s whiskers twitched. He peeked out, nose sniffing. He was ready.

They followed the soft chiming through fern-lit woods. Moonlight made the fronds glow like little emerald lamps. Tobin’s boots crunched gently on moss. Once the sound hid behind a waterfall’s mist. Once it giggled from a hollow stump, and Squeaky hopped out of the pocket to peek, then hopped back in with a crumb of moss on his nose and no bell at all.

Ding-dong! But not from here.

Very close now, beside a patch of bright bluebells that nodded as if in greeting. And there, sitting on a sun-dappled mossy log, was a witch named Willow. Her basket brimmed with leafy flowery things that smelled sweet and earthy, like a hug from the forest itself. A sprig of chamomile stuck from one side. A ribbon of river-mint from the other.

“Hello there, young wizard,” Willow said. Her smile crinkled the corners of her kind eyes. “I hear you’re looking for a wandering bell. That curious tinkling has been dancing through my herbs for the last hour, tickling their leaves.”

Tobin explained, earnest. “It rings everywhere, but I don’t know where it’s supposed to be. It’s like it’s forgotten its home.”

Willow nodded and stroked her chin. “That’s a lost Hush-a-Bye Bell. It usually rests beside the sleepy river, where the water whispers lullabies to the stones. It has been getting a bit lost and has liked to wander. It needs a special song to remind it of its proper place.”

“A song?” Tobin’s eyes widened. He loved songs. He loved magic even more.

“Indeed. A song as soft as moonlight on a quiet night and as sweet as dew on a strawberry blossom. You and your little friend both look ready to help. I can see you have very kind hearts.”

Willow showed them a little rhyme, a gentle melody that seemed to float on the air. She hummed it once, then again, until Tobin’s mouth knew the shape of it. Squeaky perched on Tobin’s shoulder, tiny paws in Tobin’s hair for balance, and squeaked along in his own tiny musical way.

Together they sang. Tobin’s voice was clear and bright like a morning star. Willow’s hum was deep and warm, like a happy bumblebee. And Squeaky added a brave little squeak-squeak-squeak that made the song full of courage. The bluebells nodded in time. Even the hollow log seemed to listen.

The little lost bell, which had been ringing from inside that log, chimed softly, then a little louder, and then, with a final joyous ding-dong, it floated out. The air smelled of fresh water and damp moss. Moonlight glinted off its surface. It circled Tobin, Squeaky, and Willow once, a happy dance, then zipped away—not in the wrong direction this time, but toward the gentle murmuring of a faraway river.

They followed just far enough to see. The sleepy river whispered lullabies to the stones, just as Willow had said. Until finally the bell settled beside it with a contented sigh that only the three of them could hear. It did not ring from the cloud. It did not ring from the rock. It rang from the water, and then it was still.

The woods grew quiet. The only sound was wind through the trees, a peaceful song of its own. Tobin and Squeaky snuggled together, warm and happy. The practice bell on the workshop desk would wait until morning. Tonight the mountains had the right chime in the right place.

Ever since then, when moonlight painted soft shadows, they slept dreaming of bells that knew their way home.

Ding-dong. From there.
characters: Tobin (young wizard of the Moonfold Mountains), Squeaky (tiny grey mouse)
